target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909) — the conflict lives in the session-store optimistic-commit path above any model runtime, so the wedge is runtime-agnostic by construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks — a runtime-agnostic fan-out where each runtime releases its own lane and clears its stale native thread binding. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | `staleSnapshotRetried` | `conflictRecoveryAttempted` | Action |
|-------|------------------------|------------------------------|--------|
| First conflict | `false` | any | `stale-snapshot-retry` — re-read store, retry commit (unchanged) |
| Second conflict | `true` | `false` | **`self-heal-retry`** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + reset harness, then retry (new) |
| Third conflict | `true` | `true` | `fail` — throw with clear context instead of silent wedge |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses. This ensures:
- A genuinely active concurrent turn is interrupted and **drained** before teardown, not disposed mid-flight
- An obsolete conflict candidate (resolved by a competing turn during drain) skips teardown entirely
- Draining runs OUTSIDE the store-write lock to avoid deadlocking an owner that must write to release

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message in a session fails → "reply session initialization conflicted" → session permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` or fresh session recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes the wedged runtime and retries → init completes → session recovers automatically → user never notices the transient conflict

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (4/4 passed)

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Integration Tests (2/2 passed) — forced double-conflict recovery

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/issue-102020-self-heal.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

- **unwedges the session via self-heal**: Forces 4 consecutive CAS conflicts → verifies init completes (sessionId preserved), wedged MCP runtime disposed, commit accounting correct (5 attempts: main stale-retry + self-heal request + fenced revalidation 2 + final success)
- **throws after self-heal budget exhausted**: Forces 6 conflicts (exceeds budget) → verifies error message includes "after harness self-heal retry"

### Existing Tests — No Regressions

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  136 passed (136)

$ pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.reply-init-concurrency.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  71 passed (71)
```

### Gateway Runtime Verification

```
$ pnpm openclaw gateway --allow-unconfigured --auth none --bind loopback
→ Gateway started successfully, ran 20s without crash
→ All modified modules (session.ts + reply-session-init-conflict.ts) loaded without import/runtime errors
```

### Bug Reproduction (pre-fix)

The CAS revision guard compares `{sessionId, sessionFile}` between snapshot load and commit. When concurrent background activity (Codex harness transcript mirror, heartbeat context tracking) modifies these identity fields between turns, both the original commit and the stale-snapshot retry fail:

```
✓ First message commit: OK
  Second commit: ok=false reason=stale-snapshot  ← CAS rejected
  Retry commit:  ok=false reason=stale-snapshot  ← still rejected
💥 "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanent wedge
```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): pure decision helper `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` with 3-state state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests covering all state transitions
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: imports decision helper; adds `conflict-self-heal` outcome type; routes conflict recovery through lifecycle mutation fence in `initSessionStateAttempt`; adds `selfHealReplySessionInitConflict()` that disposes wedged runtime + resets harness under the safety fence; replaces `throw` in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` with the 3-action conflict resolution
